correctness.rationale: For T_n=L(K_n), n>=4, induced P3 endpoints are two disjoint original graph edges and middle vertices are four crossed edges. If no disjoint selected pair then S is already fixed; if a matching of size 2 is selected, the first parallel round fills K4 on its support and attaches every other supported vertex to at least two core vertices; the second fills every supported edge. The only missing edges after one round are between vertices both originally of degree 1 with identical neighbor (a cherry), giving sharp 2-round criterion and n=4 exception. Pairwise intersecting 2-subsets are stars or triangles; otherwise full cliques occur. By cover analysis the lattice is ranked by star cardinality or clique support, with R_n=1+C(n,2)t+3C(n,3)t²+sum_{r=3}^n(n-r+1)C(n,r)t^r. Summation gives (n+2)2^(n-1)-n(n+1); atomic crosscut gives mu=(-1)^n; binomial product gives strict log-concavity. Joins of atoms recover T_n adjacency, yielding Aut(S_n) for n>=5 and S2 wr S3 order48 at n=4. Independently exhausted 33,856 initial edge subsets n=4,5,6 against predicted full closure and closed-set count, plus Möbius n=4,5. Finite census corroborates but the all-n proof is combinatorial.

The original 2013 full transcription and original 2022 arXiv HTML relevant definitions and main characterization were inspected: neither states these exact triangular-graph two-round/cherry, rank/Möbius/log-concavity or automorphism invariants.
